results.term_definition: Trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) are a class of small objects and dwarf planets that orbit the Sun beyond the orbit of Neptune. These are defined as having a typical distance from the Sun (the semi-major axis of their orbit) that is greater than Neptune's typical distance from the Sun (30.1 astronomical units or Earth–Sun distances). There are over 2000 known TNOs. Most are members of the Kuiper Belt although more distant objects are members of a population called the scattered disk.
